title: Microsoft Purview DLP: show remote machine information for file copies to Remote Desktop
summary: Hold: the PowerShell reference confirms a general Endpoint DLP parameter but does not establish that the printed call configures RDP restrictions. The briefing also omits Windows Server prerequisites and incorrectly says the parameter reference gives only its type. The roadmap facts and the cautiously stated gaps about the new information check out.

claims.claim: Endpoint DLP's Copy or move using RDP detects attempts to copy an item to a remote desktop session.
claims.quote: Copy or move using RDP | Detects when a user attempts to copy an item to a remote desktop session.

claims.claim: The RDP activity is supported on onboarded Windows 10, Windows 11 and Windows Server 2019 and later devices without further stated qualifications.
claims.quote: By default, Endpoint DLP isn't enabled for Windows servers when they're initially onboarded. Before you can see Endpoint DLP events for your servers in Activity Explorer, you must first Enable Endpoint DLP for Windows Servers.
claims.fix: Qualify the Windows Server statement in What's changing and Scope: 'Windows servers require Enable Endpoint DLP for Windows Servers after onboarding; Domain Controllers and Server Core installations are not supported.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/endpoint-dlp-learn-about. This qualifies the existing activity, not the new item's coverage.

claims.claim: Copy or move using RDP is not supported on macOS.

claims.claim: Activity explorer receives its activity information from the Microsoft 365 unified audit logs.
claims.quote: The activity information comes from the Microsoft 365 unified audit logs. It's transformed and then made available in the activity explorer UI.

claims.claim: Activity explorer is not real time.
claims.quote: Activity explorer isn't a real-time view. Because its data comes from the Microsoft 365 unified audit log, activities appear on the same schedule as audit records — not the moment they occur.

claims.claim: DLP alerts also draw on telemetry that first enters the Microsoft 365 audit logs.
claims.quote: The telemetry goes into the Microsoft 365 audit Logs first, is processed, and makes its way to different reporting tools.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-learn-about-dlp#viewing-policy-application-results to sources for the statement that DLP alerts draw on the audit log.

claims.claim: The printed Microsoft Purview custom-policy path reaches the Copy or move using RDP activity control.
claims.quote: Select Full directory under Admin units. Scope the location to Devices only. Create a rule where: ... In Actions: Select Audit or restrict activities on devices. ... Select Apply restrictions to specific activity ... Copy or move using RDP
claims.fix: Restore the omitted scope choices: 'Data Loss Prevention > Policies > Create policy > Enterprise applications & devices > Custom > Custom policy > Admin units > Full directory > Devices > rule > Actions > Audit or restrict activities on devices > Apply restrictions to specific activity > Copy or move using RDP'. Keep the note that this follows the custom-policy example, not its scan-failure condition.

claims.claim: Set-DlpComplianceRule -Identity <ComplianceRuleIdParameter> -EndpointDlpRestrictions <PswsHashtable[]> is documented as the automation for auditing or restricting RDP copies.
claims.quote: Searched: EndpointDlpRestrictions RDP; EndpointDlpRestrictions RemoteDesktop Rdp Setting; RDP Set-DlpComplianceRule. Opened Set-DlpComplianceRule, Get-PolicyConfig and Set-PolicyConfig; parameters exist, but no RDP setting mapping or statement that this operation sets the RDP control.
claims.fix: Set controls[0].api to null. The reference documents general Endpoint DLP restrictions but does not document the setting that selects Copy or move using RDP. Do not invent a Setting value or describe the generic parameter as a verified RDP operation.

claims.claim: Set-DlpComplianceRule is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.claim: The Set-DlpComplianceRule reference gives only the EndpointDlpRestrictions parameter type.
claims.quote: The EndpointDlpRestrictions parameter specifies the restricted endpoints for Endpoint DLP. This parameter uses the following syntax: @(@{"Setting"="<Setting>"; "Value"="<Value>"},...). The available values for <Value> are: Audit, Block, Ignore, or Warn.
claims.fix: Remove 'the reference gives the parameter type only' from controls[0].note and its rendered table note. The current reference gives syntax, action values, examples and an Entra role requirement, although it does not identify the RDP Setting value.
